title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: Context: Grothendieck is building the stratification 'at infinity' of the Deligne–Mumford compactification of M_{g,ν}. Strata are indexed by dual graphs G. S is the set of vertices; I is the set of half-edges and legs; Î_α is the set of half-edges and legs at vertex α; g_α is the genus attached to α. A 'standard G-épinglée' curve over a base 𝕊 is a family whose dual graph is rigidified (marked) by G. On the previous page he established the equivalence (21): M_G(𝕊) ≃ ∏_{α∈S} M_{g_α,Î_α}(𝕊). The family is obtained by normalizing along the nodes: one gets a disjoint union of smooth pointed curves Y_α, with the preimages of the nodes as extra marked points. This page adds three things. (i) The equivalence is compatible with base change, so it is an equivalence of fibred groupoids (stacks) over schemes. It is also natural in G, i.e. functorial for isomorphisms of graphs (transport de structure). (ii) Consequently the stack 𝕊 ↦ M_G(𝕊) is 2-representable by a 'schematic extension' (an algebraic stack of Deligne–Mumford type, in his language a 'multiplicité schématique') iff each factor M_{g_α,Î_α} is. This holds iff each type (g_α, ν̂_α), with ν̂_α = |Î_α|, is 'anabelian', i.e. 2g_α − 2 + ν̂_α > 0. The excluded cases are (0,0), (0,1), (0,2), (1,0); their moduli groupoids have positive-dimensional automorphism groups, so they are not DM. This is exactly the stability condition on the graph. (iii) For connected G this says G is an 'MD-graphe' (Mumford–Deligne graph = stable graph in modern terms). He then names M_G the corresponding modular multiplicity. On the next page this becomes M_{[G]} = (M_G, Aut G), i.e. the stack quotient [∏ M_{g_α,n_α} / Aut G]. That is the modular stack of stable curves of combinatorial type [G], i.e. the locally closed boundary stratum.
errors: No real error. The 'iff' is fine because every factor is non-empty, so the product is DM iff each factor is.

'2-représentable par une extension schématique' must be read as representable by a DM-type multiplicity. In the non-anabelian cases M_{0,2} and M_{1,0} are still algebraic (Artin) stacks, just not DM. M_{0,0} and M_{0,1} are also Artin stacks with positive-dimensional automorphism groups.

ideas.what: Boundary stratum of stable curves of type G identified with a product of moduli of smooth pointed curves, via normalization at the nodes
ideas.modern_name: Gluing/clutching description of strata: M_G ≅ ∏_v M_{g(v),n(v)}, stratum = [M_G/Aut G]
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne–Mumford (1969), Knudsen (1983); systematized by Kontsevich–Manin and Getzler–Kapranov (modular operads, 1998)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the 'structure à l'infini' and the Mumford–Deligne compactification, but not in this explicit form

ideas.what: Representability (DM) of the stratum stack iff every vertex type is anabelian (2g−2+n>0), i.e. iff the graph is stable
ideas.where_published: The 'anabelian type' (2g−2+ν>0) terminology appears in Esquisse d'un programme

ideas.what: Term 'MD-graphe' for connected stable graphs, and 'multiplicité modulaire' M_G with Aut G acting
ideas.modern_name: Stable graph; moduli stack of the stratum; Aut(G)-quotient

deep.surprise_reason: Routine and correct bookkeeping of the standard product decomposition of boundary strata, plus the stability criterion. The only mildly distinctive features are the terminology ('MD-graphe', 'anabélien' types, 'multiplicité') and the early stack-theoretic framing. Nothing absent from the literature.
